findings.certainty: READ; not run, not reproduced. gui/mod.rs dwell_pending_ms (in the new impl block, 'fn dwell_pending_ms'), GuiFrame::advance (the dwell part after 'if self.agent { return; }'), dwell_reset (:2895-2917), panel_at (:907-924), window.rs wait_flow and gui_settled.
findings.severity: medium (Operator window only; a periodic no-op wake, at worst every 1 ms; a non-quiet framed run can end in Timeout)
findings.where: hsk-studio-native-host/src/gui/mod.rs dwell_pending_ms; src/window.rs wait_flow (ControlFlow::WaitUntil) and gui_settled
findings.what: dwell_pending_ms does not use the same conditions as advance. It reads menu.dwell_ms without checking that the hovered control is menu.dwell_target, and it does not know dwell_reset's on_tip early return. When an L0 tip of control A shows and the pointer moves into the tip rect over another control B (panel_at gives the band under a tip, so hovered = B), dwell_reset returns at on_tip: dwell_target stays A and dwell_ms stays frozen in [400, 900). dwell_pending_ms then answers Some(900 - dwell_ms) for B on every call. advance does not add to dwell_ms (hovered != dwell_target), so if B has no tip record or no place (tip_record or tip_place None) nothing changes and the same deadline is returned again.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator rests the pointer inside a shown L0 tip over a control without a tip: the window wakes every (900 - dwell_ms) ms, between 1 ms and 500 ms, for as long as the pointer rests there, each wake running gui_tick. A non-quiet window run with --frames whose script leaves the pointer there never reaches gui_settled and exits 6 (Timeout).
findings.fix: Make dwell_pending_ms answer None when hovered != menu.dwell_target or when the pointer is inside a shown tip's rect, and None when tip_record or tip_place of the wanted level is None. Add a frame test (CPU, cheap): after advance(next_timer_ms()) the pending time is None or strictly smaller, looped at most 4 times, for a pointer on a control with a tip, without a tip, and inside a tip rect.

findings.what: Accumulation is exact for plain and Shift steps (multiples of 0.5). Under Ctrl the per-px step is 0.05, which f64 cannot hold, and settle rounds at 0.1: a value that lands on a half quantum (99.95, 99.85) rounds up or down by accumulated error, so the same net displacement can commit values 0.1 apart depending on the sample count, and a drag and SetValue of the same literal can differ by 0.1. Test 4 does not pin the value after 500 samples: it compares the document to the field's own shown value (want = shown(&f)), so drift would pass. Test 6 compares only plain-step drags.
findings.failure_scenario: Ctrl-drag 3 px in one sample versus three samples: 99.85 by two paths, one commits 99.9 and one 99.8.
findings.fix: Accumulate in integer units of step/10 quanta (or keep the logical-px sum and multiply once), then settle. A new test in a new commit: after the 500 samples of test 4 the value is 74.5 (net dx -49, dy +2); a Ctrl drag of N px in 1 sample and in N samples commits the same value. Do not edit test 4 (ruling 11).

answers.arbiter: Pointer capture: wheel, every key but Escape, every other button, invoke (pointer_owned) and set_value (pointer_owned) are refused or ignored while a drag owns the pointer; PointerLeft is ignored during a drag. Outside the client area the raw position still drives motion (pointer None, raw kept). Modifiers are read from the frame's mods at each sample; window.rs lands the pending move before a Modifiers event. Clamp at each sample (gesture.rs:201-207). Escape: value back, pointer held to release, no commit. Focus loss COMMITS a drag or wheel transaction once (finalize), as the deliberation and STU-SHL-194 say; it does not abort. A refused commit writes no step and the field shows the document value. A click without movement and a zero net change count `unchanged` and commit nothing. One commit per gesture by construction (take() on release, finalize and close_wheel). Selection cannot change during a drag; during a wheel transaction every route that changes selection (press, key, invoke, pointer leaving the field) closes the transaction on the captured target first.
answers.host_clock: Order fix is right by reading. Quiet runs: set_agent_driven(args.quiet) and offscreen set_agent_driven(true); advance returns before the dwell in agent mode; frame test agent_mode_has_no_dwell_tip covers it. Exit and capture wait on gui_settled within the deadline (tick :694 Timeout), so a run cannot exit with a gesture timer pending and cannot wait unbounded. The Operator window uses Wait or WaitUntil(next timer), never Poll. A quiet run keeps its existing Poll and presents during the up to 400 ms idle wait (bounded). Offscreen settles at script end, so both end in the same committed frame; the gui_window and gui_vulkan tests that compare them were not in the focused run.
answers.actor_sites: Production GuiFrame open sites: offscreen.rs:75 and window.rs:344, both open_as with host.actor(). GuiFrame::open is pub, test-only by its doc, with no production caller. Default caller by design: cli.rs:118 (no --actor) and studio-vk.rs:45 (the failure frame after a caller-argument refusal).
